Per Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J. :
1. Heard Mr. Vijayant Verma, learned counsel for the appellant and Mr. Mukesh Kumar learned counsel appearing for the respondent.

2. This appeal is directed against the judgement and decree dated 07.02.2019 (decree signed on 13.02.2019) passed by Sri Peeyush Kumar, learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Bokaro in Original Suit No. 385/2015
whereby and whereunder, the suit preferred by the appellant for dissolution of his marriage with the respondent has been dismissed.

(Against The Judgment And Decree Dated ... vs Archana Kumari on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195443076/
1
3. For the sake of convenience, both the parties are referred to in this judgment as per their status before the learning trial court.

4. The petitioner (appellant herein) had preferred a suit for Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB dissolution of marriage with the respondent/wife (respondent herein) in which it has been stated that the marriage of the petitioner was solemnised with the respondent on 29.04.2007 as per Hindu rites and customs and after marriage, the respondent went to reside at her matrimonial house.
Out of the said wedlock, a child was born on 30.06.2008.

After the marriage, the behaviour of the respondent towards the petitioner and her in- laws was not cordial and the respondent used to frequently visit her parental house and whenever the petitioner had tried to bring back the respondent, he was met with a stiff resistance from the family members of the respondent.
The respondent, despite the query of the petitioner regarding her stay at her parental house, did not submit any explanation.
It has been stated that the respondent always behaved in a cruel manner with the petitioner and she did not want to spend her conjugal life with the petitioner.

When the frequent visits of the respondent to her parental house was objected by the petitioner and his family members, the respondent used to threaten them of implicating the entire family members in a criminal case.
The parents of the respondent did not respond to the plea of the petitioner for attempting to change the behaviour of the respondent towards the petitioner.

The respondent has lastly come to her matrimonial house on 30.06.2009 to celebrate the birthday party of her son and after staying for a week, she left the house on 13.07.2009 and after that she never came back to her matrimonial house.
The respondent in course of leaving her matrimonial house had also taken away the jewelries and cloths given to her by her in-laws.
It has been stated that there has been no cohabitation between the petitioner and the respondent since the year 2008.

5. On being noticed, the respondent had appeared and filed her written statement in which she has denied the allegations Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB levelled by the petitioner in his application seeking divorce.

Despite the family member of the respondent giving cash and other items at the time of marriage, the petitioner at the instance of his parents after 6 months of the marriage, had demanded a golden ring and Rs. 2 lakhs in cash and on refusal, the petitioner and his family members had tortured the respondent in various manners and they also did not provide proper clothes and food to the respondent.
The father of the respondent had given Rs. 50,000/- on seeing the plight of the respondent and during this period, a son was born on 30.06.2009.
The respondent has always been very cooperative towards the petitioner and his family members and she is ready to spend her conjugal life with the petitioner with respect and honour.

It has been stated that the petitioner had ousted the respondent and her infant child from her matrimonial house for which a maintenance case was filed by the respondent being M.P. No. 125/2009 before the Principal Judge, Family Court, Bokaro and on intervention by the Court, the respondent had gone to her matrimonial house on 05.08.2010, but there was no change in the behaviour of the petitioner and his family members.

The petitioner had filed a suit for restitution of conjugal rights being T.M.S. No.
183/2010 and the respondent was in her matrimonial house, but she was not allowed to attend the dates in the said suit.

On 20.12.2010, the respondent was working in the kitchen when the petitioner (Against The Judgment And Decree Dated ... vs Archana Kumari on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195443076/
2 and his family members abused and assaulted her and after snatching her ornaments, had ousted her from her matrimonial house.
The respondent has filed a criminal case on 21.05.2011 in the Court of C.J.M., Bokaro being C.P. No. 267/2011 against the petitioner and his family members which is still pending.

It has been stated that during the pendency of C.P. 267/2011, the petitioner had filed an undertaking to keep the respondent with him with full dignity and honour consequent to which the Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB respondent went to reside at her matrimonial house on 12.03.2014, but the petitioner did not treat her with respect and lastly had dropped the respondent at Bokaro.

There is no cause of action for the suit as the date of bidai is 12.03.2014,
while the suit was filed on 14.07.2014 and the period of separation is less than a year.
6. Based on the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed for adjudication:
1.
Whether the suit as framed maintainable?
2. Whether the petitioner has valid cause of action for the present suit?
3. Whether the respondent treated the petitioner with cruelty?
4. Whether the respondent deserted the petitioner for more than two years before the presentation of the present suit?
5. Whether the marriage solemnised between the petitioner and the respondent on 29.04.2007 can be dissolved?
6. Whether the petitioner is entitled to the relief prayed for?

7. The petitioner (appellant herein) has examined four witnesses on his behalf:
P.W.1 Sukhdeo Sharma is the father of the petitioner who has stated about the solemnisation of marriage of the petitioner on 29.04.2007 at Bokaro Steel City and on 30.06.2008, the couple were blessed with a child.
After the marriage, the behaviour of the respondent towards the petitioner and his family members were not good and she frequently used to go to her parental house.
He has stated that after marriage, the respondent most of the time used to reside at her parental house.

Whenever he and his family members tried to bring the Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB respondent back to her matrimonial house, her parents and siblings opposed such move and did not allow her to go back to her matrimonial house.
The respondent never disclosed the reason for her reluctance to stay at her matrimonial house.
During her stay at her matrimonial house, the behaviour of the respondent was cruel and she disliked the petitioner and never wanted to lead a conjugal life with him.
Whenever he and the others objected to the frequent visits of the respondent to her parental house, she always used to issue threats of implicating them in false cases.

He had met the parents of the respondent and requested them to counsel their daughter so that she can lead a peaceful marital life with the petitioner (Against The Judgment And Decree Dated ... vs Archana Kumari on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195443076/
3 but the same did not have any effect.
The respondent had last come to his place on 30.06.2009 to celebrate her son's birthday and on 13.07.2009 she had left never to return back.
He has stated that on 05.07.2014 he had appeared in Court with his son in Complaint Case No. 267/2011 and his son was assaulted by the respondent and her father.

When despite repeated efforts, the respondent did not come back to her matrimonial house, the petitioner had instituted a suit for restitution of conjugal rights and despite receipt of summons, the respondent did not appear in the said suit.
In May 2011, the respondent had instituted a false case under Section 498A IPC against him and his family members which is at present pending.

He and his wife are aged persons who does not keep well and since the respondent did not want to stay with them, the petitioner had kept her in a rented house, but the respondent had left the said place without any information.

In the criminal case, on the orders of the Court, the respondent was brought to her matrimonial house but when they reached Bokaro Station from Ranchi, the respondent had called her father and brother to the station and he and his family members were abused and humiliated and they had taken with Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB them the respondent to her parental house.
He has stated that the respondent had instituted a case of maintenance and as per the order, maintenance amount is being extended to the respondent.
In cross-examination, he has deposed that only the respondent had instituted a case against him and not his younger daughter-in-law.
From 2009 to 2014, the respondent had come to his house 3-4 times.
It is true that in C.P. Case No. 267/2011, an undertaking was given by the petitioner on 12.03.2014 to keep the respondent and her child with full dignity and honour.
The respondent used to express her dislike for the petitioner.
The petitioner wanted to keep the respondent, but the petitioner used to disclose to him that the respondent has an illicit affair with a person named Rajeshwar Rai.
However, he has not mentioned about the said fact in his sworn statement.
The petitioner has also not mentioned about the illicit affair with Rajeshwar Rai.
He has also taken assistance from his neighbours to ensure that the petitioner and the respondent stay together, but the respondent always used to resort to violence.
He had not informed about such violence to either the Police or to the administration.
He had not undergone any treatment for the assault committed by the respondent on 05.07.2014.
A case was instituted under Section 107 Cr.P.C. for the act of assault but he had never appeared in the said case.
After the suit for restitution was filed, the respondent had gone to stay with the petitioner.
He had not allowed her to enter his house.
He does not want to keep the respondent with him.

P.W.2 Satish Sharma is the petitioner who has stated that his marriage was solemnised with the respondent on 29-04-2007 as per Hindu rites and customs and out of the said wedlock, a son was born on 30.06.2008.
The behaviour of the respondent after marriage was cruel towards him and towards his family Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB members.
She used to frequently go to her parents' place and in fact, most of the time, she resided at her parents' place.
Whenever he tried to bring back the respondent, it was met with stiff resistance by her parents and siblings.
He had wanted to know the reason for the respondent not to stay at her matrimonial house but she merely replied that she wants to stay at her parents' place.

Whenever the respondent stayed with him, her (Against The Judgment And Decree Dated ... vs Archana Kumari on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195443076/
4 behaviour was cruel and she clearly expressed her feelings that she does not like him and does not want to continue her marital life with him.
He has stated that the respondent, without any information, used to go to her parents' place and whenever he objected, she threatened of implicating them in false cases.
The respondent had come to his house for the last time on 30.06.2009 to celebrate the birthday of her son and on 13.07.2009, she had left taking with her all her belongings.
On 05.07.2014, he and his father had come to the Court to attend Complaint Case No. 267/2011 and on that day, they were subjected to assault by the respondent and her father.
This information was given to the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bokaro and B.S. City P.S. after which a proceeding was initiated under Section 107 Cr.P.C.

Despite repeated efforts, when the respondent did not come back to her matrimonial house, he was constrained to file a suit under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act for restitution of conjugal rights.
In May 2011, the respondent had lodged a case under Section 498A IPC against him and his family members which is at present pending.
He had kept the respondent in a rented house but from there also, the respondent had left without informing him.

In the criminal case, on the orders of the Court, he had brought the respondent home and had also got his son admitted in Vivekananda Vidya Mandir and when they reached Bokaro Steel City Station at 1:30AM, the brother and father of the respondent whom she had called Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB abused and humiliated him and took away the respondent with them.
On the orders of the Court, he had also gone to the parent's place of the respondent, but there also he was subjected to humiliation.
The respondent had instituted a case of maintenance and as per the order of the Court, he is regularly making payment of the amount of maintenance to the respondent.
He has produced an application of the respondent which has been marked as 'X' in which the respondent had expressed her desire to stay at her parent's place along with her son.
He has also produced an application marked 'X'/1 in which the respondent had shown her reluctance to enter into a compromise and she wants to stay with her son at her parent's place.
He had given an application to the Officer-in-charge Khunti P.S. informing about the respondent leaving his house on 05.08.2010.
This has been marked as 'X'/2.
The application given by his father on 05.07.2014 to the Court has been marked as 'X'/3, while the non-FIR No. 27/14 dated 11.07.2014 has been marked as 'X'/4.
In cross-examination, he has deposed that he works in Bajaj Allianz at Lohardaga.
He had met the respondent for the last time in his house in the year 2013 when she had come to his house on the order of the Court.
She had stayed for 28 days in his house.
It is true that on 12.03.2014 on the basis of a complaint, he had taken the respondent to his house and the respondent had stayed with him for a month.

During this period, he had got his son admitted in Vivekananda School, Dhurwa,
Ranchi.
After one month, the respondent left from the railway station with her brother to her parents' place after abusing and assaulting him.
He had gone to his in-laws' place about 5-6 times.
He had not mentioned about the illicit affair of the respondent with another person in the application for divorce since it came to his knowledge after the case was filed.
He can Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB take back the respondent and his son provided the respondent withdraws all cases instituted by her against him.
P.W.3 Saraswati Devi is the mother of the petitioner who has reiterated what has been stated by P.W.1 and P.W.2.
(Against The Judgment And Decree Dated ... vs Archana Kumari on 3 November, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195443076/
5
In cross-examination, she has deposed that if the respondent undertakes to stay peacefully, she would bring her back.
The respondent also has to withdraw all cases instituted by her.
The petitioner even today wants to keep the respondent with him.
The parents of the respondent used to regularly extend threats to her family.
P.W.4 Sidheshwar Prasad Singh is the neighbour of the petitioner and his statement is similar to that of the other witnesses.
In cross-examination, he has deposed that he knows Satish Sharma for the last 25-30 years.
He does not know as to whether the respondent is willing to go to her matrimonial house or not.
When the respondent wanted to go to her matrimonial house, the petitioner was not ready to keep her.
8. The respondent has examined three witnesses on her behalf:

R.W.1 Lal Sharma is the father of the respondent who has stated that after marriage when the respondent went to her matrimonial house, there was a demand of Rs. 2 lakhs as dowry and when the same was not fulfilled, the respondent was subjected to physical and mental torture.

A case was also instituted by the respondent being C.P.
No. 267/2011 which is pending.
In the said case, three times compromise was effected and each time when the respondent went to her matrimonial house, she was subjected to torture.
A son was born out of the said wedlock who is staying with him and studying at Class- IV in Kairali Springdale School.
He has denied that the respondent has ever committed cruelty upon her husband and in-laws.
The Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB respondent, considering her future and the future of her son, wants to stay with the petitioner.

In cross-examination, he has deposed that he had got the respondent treated by Dr.
Shobha Sinha as well as at B.G.H. and at K.M. Memorial, but he has not produced the prescriptions of such treatment.
He had got the respondent treated for gynecological related disease.
The respondent is staying with him since 2011.
The respondent will go to her matrimonial house if she is kept well.
R.W.2 Chandrakala Devi is the mother of the respondent who has reiterated what has been stated by R.W.1 in his sworn statement.

In cross-examination, she has deposed that if the bidai of the respondent is done as per the order of the Court and if she is not subjected to torture, then all the cases will be withdrawn without any condition.
R.W.3 Archana Kumari is the respondent who has stated that her marriage was solemnised with the petitioner on 29.04.2007 as per Hindu rites and customs at Bokaro.
When she went to her matrimonial house, there was a demand made of Rs. 2 lakhs and despite making a payment of Rs. 50,000/-, the torture upon her continued.
Out of the wedlock, a son was born who is at present studying in Class-IV.

She has (Against The Judgment And Decree Dated ... vs Archana Kumari on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195443076/
6 stated that the petitioner and his family members ultimately assaulted her and sent her to her parents' place for which she had instituted a case being M.P. Case No.
125/2009 before the Family Court and though on the order of the Court, she was sent to her matrimonial house, but there was no change in the behaviour of her in-laws.
She still wants to reside with her husband if she is kept with dignity and honour.

On 20-12-2010, when she was cooking food in the kitchen at her matrimonial house, the petitioner and his family members cast aspersion upon her Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB character and had also abused and assaulted her.
Due to the torture committed upon her, she had instituted C.P. 267/2011 which is presently pending in Bokaro.

In course of the proceedings of C.P. 267/2011, on the basis of an undertaking given by the petitioner, she had gone to her matrimonial house on 12.03.2014, but she was again subjected to torture and on 14.07.2014, the suit for dissolution of marriage was instituted by the petitioner.
She has denied to have misbehaved or committed physical and mental cruelty upon the petitioner and his family members.
She had, on several occasions, expressed her desire to go back to her matrimonial house, but the same could not fructify due to the adamant attitude of her in-laws.
She has stated that she is ready to reignite her marital life if she is kept with full honour and dignity.
She has proved the order sheet dated 12.03.2014 in C.P. Case No. 267/2011 which has been marked as Exhibit-A.
She has proved the compromise in which the signature of both parties are present which has been marked as Exhibit-B.
She has also proved the certified copy of the cross- examination of Sukhdeo Sharma in M.P. No. 125/2009 which has been marked as Exhibit-C.

The certified copies of the cross- examination of Sidheswar Prasad Singh and Satish Sharma in M.P. No.
125/2009 have been marked as Exhibit-D and E respectively.
In cross-examination, she has deposed that she has lodged four cases against the petitioner.
She is staying separate from the petitioner since 0507.2014.
She had gone to her matrimonial house on three occasions on the orders of the Court.
In the criminal case, the petitioner had to go to jail.
She is ready to withdraw all the cases instituted by her and go to her matrimonial house along with her son.
She has not filed any prescription regarding her treatment as well as the treatment of her son.
Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB 9.

It has been submitted by Mr. Vijayant Verma, learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant that the learned trial court has not properly appreciated the cruelty meted out by the respondent and has discussed the evidence of the petitioner in a cursory manner.

The respondent has admitted that she has filed four cases against the petitioner who had also gone to jail in connection with the criminal case and the same itself tantamounts to cruelty inflicted upon the petitioner by the respondent.
The tenor of the evidence of the respondent and her witnesses highlights the desire of the respondent not to resume her marital life with the petitioner.

The ingredients of animus deserendi is made out and desertion can be inferred from the fact that the respondent had refused to discharge her matrimonial obligation which amounts to abandonment of marriage.

It has been submitted by Mr.
Verma that the various instances propagated by the petitioner clearly indicates that a case of (Against The Judgment And Decree Dated ... vs Archana Kumari on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195443076/
7
dissolution of marriage is made out and, therefore, the impugned judgement is liable to be set aside.

10. Mr. Mukesh Kumar, learned counsel appearing for the respondent has submitted that the respondent had left her matrimonial house not out of desire but out of compulsion on account of the incessant torture meted out to her; the cases lodged by the respondent against the petitioner being a confirmation of the same.

The respondent has repeatedly expressed her desire to stay with the petitioner and even the undertaking given by the petitioner before the Court has not been adhered to which has totally denuded the case of the petitioner.
11. We have heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and have also perused the trial court records.
12. The suit had been preferred by the petitioner on the ground of "cruelty" and "desertion".
Cruelty has not been defined in the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 but has evolved with time which are Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB reflected in the various judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
In Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh reported in (2007) 4 SCC 511, it has been held as follows:

entities.text: Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh reported in (2007) 4 SCC 511
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: " 99. Human mind is extremely complex and human behaviour is equally complicated.
Similarly human ingenuity has no bound, therefore, to assimilate the entire human behaviour in one definition is almost impossible.
What is cruelty in one case may not amount to cruelty in other case.

The concept of cruelty differs from person to person depending upon his upbringing, level of sensitivity, educational,
family and cultural background, financial position, social status, customs, traditions,
religious beliefs, human values and their value system.

100. Apart from this, the concept of mental cruelty cannot remain static; it is bound to change with the passage of time, impact of modern culture through print and electronic media and value system, etc. etc.
What may be mental cruelty now may not remain a mental cruelty after a passage of time or vice versa.
There can never be any straitjacket formula or fixed parameters for determining mental cruelty in matrimonial matters.
The prudent and appropriate way to adjudicate the case would be to evaluate it on its peculiar facts and circumstances while taking aforementioned factors in consideration."
Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB 13.

The petitioner in his evidence as P.W.1 has stated about the respondent resorting to a cruel behaviour towards him and his family members after marriage and for no reasons whatsoever the respondent used to visit her parental house where she remained for long durations.

Instances have also been sought to be highlighted that despite several efforts made by the petitioner, the respondent as well as her family members were reluctant in restoring the marital ties and the petitioner was also subjected to abuses, humiliation and assault.

In course of trial, the father of the petitioner examined as P.W.1 has introduced a new story of the respondent having an illicit relationship with one Rajeshwar Rai which information he had received from the petitioner and the (Against The Judgment And Decree Dated ... vs Archana Kumari on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195443076/
8
petitioner has also reiterated such allegations.

The respondent on the other hand has denied all the allegations and has put forward the reasons for her leaving her matrimonial house attributed to the mental and physical torture committed upon her leading to institution of a plethora of cases.

14. So far as cruelty is concerned, the same are vague and unsubstantiated and the allegations do not resonate a situation making it an impossibility for the petitioner to continue with his marital life with the respondent.

In fact, the willingness of the petitioner to restore normalcy in the marital life is reflected in the undertaking given by the petitioner in the complaint case instituted by the respondent, but despite such undertaking, as per the respondent (R.W.3), the torture resumed which forced her to leave her matrimonial house.

The evidence of R.W.3 which categorises the reasons for the respondent in leaving her matrimonial house greatly diminishes the case of the petitioner seeking dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty.

The respondent, however,
despite all such sufferings has expressed her desire to restore marital life with the petitioner on the condition that she is extended proper care and dignity by the Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB petitioner.

The petitioner has not only been unable to prove the allegations of cruelty but has also made a belated and unsubstantiated allegation against the respondent of having an illicit affair with one Rajeshwar Rai.
The learned court below has, therefore, rightly rejected the claim of the petitioner that he was treated with cruelty.
15. The other ground which has been taken by the petitioner is of desertion.

In the case of DebanandaTamuli v. Kakumoni Kataky reported in (2022) 5 SCC 459, it has been held as follows:
"7.

entities.text: DebanandaTamuli v. Kakumoni Kataky reported in (2022) 5 SCC 459
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We have given careful consideration to her submissions.
Firstly, we deal with the issue of desertion.

The learned counsel appearing for the appellant relied upon the decision of this Court in Lachman Utamchand Kirpalani [Lachman Utamchand Kirpalani v. Meena, (1964) 4 SCR 331 : AIR 1964 SC 40] which has been consistently followed in several decisions of this Court.

entities.text: Lachman Utamchand Kirpalani [Lachman Utamchand Kirpalani v. Meena, (1964) 4 SCR 331 : AIR 1964 SC 40]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The law consistently laid down by this Court is that desertion means the intentional abandonment of one spouse by the other without the consent of the other and without a reasonable cause.
The deserted spouse must prove that there is a factum of separation and there is an intention on the part of deserting spouse to bring the cohabitation to a permanent end.
In other words, there should be animus deserendi on the part of the deserting spouse.

There must be an absence of consent on the part of the deserted spouse and the conduct of the Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB deserted spouse should not give a reasonable cause to the deserting spouse to leave the matrimonial home.

The view taken by this Court has been incorporated in the Explanation added to sub-section (1)
of Section 13 by Act 68 of 1976.

The said Explanation reads thus:
"13. Divorce.(1) * * * Explanation.--

In this sub-section, the expression "desertion"
means the desertion of the petitioner by the other party to the marriage without reasonable cause and without the consent or against the wish of such party, and includes the wilful neglect of the petitioner by the other party to the marriage, and its grammatical variations and cognate expressions shall be construed accordingly."
(Against The Judgment And Decree Dated ... vs Archana Kumari on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195443076/
9 16.
In the present case, the respondent has given several instances of she being forced to leave her matrimonial house, the predominant feature being of torture committed upon her.

If at all there was a willful abandonment on the part of the respondent with an intention to bring the cohabitation to a permanent end, there would not have been efforts made to make an attempt to restore marital life which can be fathomed from the undertaking given by the petitioner in the complaint case.
This would further get enhanced by the desire shown by the respondent in her evidence as R.W.3.

The repeated leaving of the matrimonial house by the respondent can be attributed to the act of the petitioner and his family members and not to any intentional abandonment of the petitioner by the respondent.
The learned Neutral Citation 2025:JHHC:32919-DB trial court has correctly decided the issue of desertion against the petitioner and in favour of the respondent.

17. Thus, on the basis of the discussions made hereinabove, we do not find any reason to interfere in the impugned judgement and decree dated 07.02.2019 (decree signed on 13.02.2019) passed by Sri Peeyush Kumar, learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Bokaro in Original Suit No. 385/2015 and consequently, we hereby dismiss this appeal.
18. Pending I.A.s, if any, stands closed.
(RONGON MUKHOPADHYAY, J.)

(PRADEEP KUMAR SRIVASTAVA, J.) Jharkhand High Court,
Ranchi Dated the 3rd Day of November, 2025 Preet/N.A.F.R.

Out of the said wedlock, a child was born on 30.06.2008.

The parents of the respondent did not respond to the plea of the petitioner for attempting to change the behaviour of the respondent towards the petitioner.
The petitioner had filed a suit for restitution of conjugal rights being T.M.S. No.

The respondent has filed a criminal case on 21.05.2011 in the Court of C.J.M., Bokaro being C.P. No. 267/2011 against the petitioner and his family members which is still pending.
The respondent never disclosed the reason for her reluctance to stay at her matrimonial house.
During her stay at her matrimonial house, the behaviour of the respondent was cruel and she disliked the petitioner and never wanted to lead a conjugal life with him.
When despite repeated efforts, the respondent did not come back to her matrimonial house, the petitioner had instituted a suit for restitution of conjugal rights and despite receipt of summons, the respondent did not appear in the said suit.
In May 2011, the respondent had instituted a false case under Section 498A IPC against him and his family members which is at present pending.
He and his wife are aged persons who does not keep well and since the respondent did not want to stay with them, the petitioner had kept her in a rented house, but the respondent had left the said place without any information.
A case was instituted under Section 107 Cr.P.C. for the act of assault but he had never appeared in the said case.
After the suit for restitution was filed, the respondent had gone to stay with the petitioner.
He had not allowed her to enter his house.
He does not want to keep the respondent with him.
The respondent had come to his house for the last time on 30.06.2009 to celebrate the birthday of her son and on 13.07.2009, she had left taking with her all her belongings.
On 05.07.2014, he and his father had come to the Court to attend Complaint Case No. 267/2011 and on that day, they were subjected to assault by the respondent and her father.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
In the criminal case, the petitioner had to go to jail.
The tenor of the evidence of the respondent and her witnesses highlights the desire of the respondent not to resume her marital life with the petitioner.
The ingredients of animus deserendi is made out and desertion can be inferred from the fact that the respondent had refused to discharge her matrimonial obligation which amounts to abandonment of marriage.
dissolution of marriage is made out and, therefore, the impugned judgement is liable to be set aside.
The respondent has repeatedly expressed her desire to stay with the petitioner and even the undertaking given by the petitioner before the Court has not been adhered to which has totally denuded the case of the petitioner.
12. The suit had been preferred by the petitioner on the ground of "cruelty" and "desertion".
The learned counsel appearing for the appellant relied upon the decision of this Court in Lachman Utamchand Kirpalani [Lachman Utamchand Kirpalani v. Meena, (1964) 4 SCR 331 : AIR 1964 SC 40] which has been consistently followed in several decisions of this Court.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In fact, the willingness of the petitioner to restore normalcy in the marital life is reflected in the undertaking given by the petitioner in the complaint case instituted by the respondent, but despite such undertaking, as per the respondent (R.W.3), the torture resumed which forced her to leave her matrimonial house.
The petitioner has not only been unable to prove the allegations of cruelty but has also made a belated and unsubstantiated allegation against the respondent of having an illicit affair with one Rajeshwar Rai.
The learned court below has, therefore, rightly rejected the claim of the petitioner that he was treated with cruelty.
